questions.question: What is the traditional attire worn by women performing Tippani dance?

options.text: Chaniya choli (traditional skirt and blouse) with ornaments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaniya choli (traditional skirt and blouse) with ornaments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tippani dance** is a vibrant folk dance originating from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, traditionally performed by women from the **Koli** and **Gola** communities.
 
• The performers wear the iconic **Chaniya choli**, which consists of a long, flared skirt called the **Chaniya** (or Ghagra) and a short, fitted blouse known as the **Choli**.
 
• This ethnic ensemble is typically made of brightly colored cotton or silk, often featuring intricate **embroidery**, mirror work, and heavy borders to reflect the cultural heritage of **Gujarat**.
 
• Accompanying the dress, women wear **traditional ornaments** such as heavy silver necklaces, chunky bangles, waistbands (Kandora), and earrings, which provide a rhythmic sound and visual appeal during the dance.
 
• A colorful **Odhni** or dupatta is draped over the head or shoulders, tucked into the waist to allow free movement while beating the **Tippani** sticks against the ground.
 
• Hence, **Chaniya choli (traditional skirt and blouse) with ornaments** is the correct attire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tippani Tool and Origin**:

 
 
• The dance is named after the **Tippani**, a wooden mallet-like tool used by construction workers in **Chorwad** and **Veraval** to level floors.
 
• It transitioned from a labor activity into a folk art where women beat the floor in a rhythmic pattern, often accompanied by instruments like the **Zanj**, **Manjira**, **Tabla**, and **Dhol**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Jewelry**:
 
 
• The **ornaments** are not merely decorative; they signify the marital status and social standing of the women in rural **Gujarati** communities.
 
• In the context of the dance, the **mirror work** on the attire catches the light, creating a shimmering effect that complements the high-energy movements of the dancers.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is rich in which type of soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deccan Plateau** is characterized by its vast stretches of **Black soil**, which is also scientifically referred to as **Regur soil**.
 
• This soil type originates from the weathering and denudation of **basaltic rocks** formed by ancient **volcanic activity** and lava flows during the **Cretaceous period**.
 
• **Black soil** is globally renowned for its high **clay content**, which grants it an exceptional capacity for **moisture retention**, crucial for agriculture in rain-fed areas.
 
• It exhibits a unique **self-ploughing** property; during the dry season, it develops deep **vertical cracks** that facilitate the oxygenation of the soil and internal drainage.
 
• Chemically, it is rich in essential plant nutrients such as **Calcium Carbonate**, **Magnesium**, **Potash**, and **Lime**, although it is typically deficient in **Phosphorous** and **Nitrogen**.
 
• Geographically, it dominates the **North-Western** part of the plateau, covering significant portions of **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and the **Malwa Plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Cotton Soil**:

 
 
• It is primarily used for the cultivation of **Cotton**, earning it the specific nomenclature **Black Cotton Soil**.
 
• Apart from cotton, it supports crops like **Sugarcane**, **Wheat**, **Linseed**, and **Sunflowers**.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil**:
 
 
• Formed by the deposition of silts by the **Himalayan rivers**. It is the most widespread soil in the **Indo-Gangetic plains** but less common in the deep **Deccan** interior.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**:
 
 
• Develops on **crystalline igneous rocks** in areas of low rainfall. Its color is due to a wide diffusion of **Iron** in crystalline and metamorphic forms.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil**:
 
 
• Formed under conditions of **high temperature** and **heavy rainfall** with alternating wet and dry periods, leading to intense **leaching** of silica and lime.

questions.question: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) has increased the focus on which type of justice system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Victim-centric and restorative justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023** was enacted to replace the **Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860**, marking a paradigm shift from a **colonial-era retributive** approach to a modern framework prioritizing **justice** over mere **punishment**.
 
• The legislation introduces **community service** as a specific form of punishment for minor offenses (such as **defamation** and **public misconduct**), which is a core component of **restorative justice** aimed at offender reform.
 
• It empowers victims by mandating that they are informed of the **investigation progress** within **90 days**, ensuring their participation and right to information throughout the legal process.
 
• Specific provisions have been strengthened to protect **women and children**, including the introduction of **life imprisonment** or the **death penalty** for **gang rape** of minors, reflecting a **victim-centric** protection model.
 
• The **BNS** facilitates easier access to justice through the introduction of **Zero FIR** and **e-FIR**, allowing victims to report crimes irrespective of the **police station's jurisdiction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colonial penal code:**

 
 
• This refers to the **Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860**, drafted by **Lord Macaulay**. It was primarily designed to safeguard **British colonial interests** and focused on maintaining **public order** through **harsh punitive measures**.
 
 
 
• **Criminal Justice Reforms:**
 
 
• The **BNS** is part of a **tripartite legal overhaul** alongside the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)** and the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**, which replace the **CrPC** and **Indian Evidence Act**.
 
• The new laws emphasize **forensic science**, making it mandatory for crimes involving punishment of **seven years or more** to ensure higher **conviction rates** and scientific accuracy in trials.
 
• **Organized crime** and **terrorism** have been clearly defined for the first time within the general penal law to address modern security challenges effectively.

questions.question: In the Mansabdari system, what term referred to the cavalrymen maintained by the Mansabdar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sawar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was the administrative framework of the **Mughal Empire**, formalized by **Emperor Akbar** around **1571** to organize the nobility and the military.
 
• Under this system, every officer was assigned a **Mansab** (rank), which was divided into two distinct components: **Zat** and **Sawar**.
 
• The term **Sawar** referred to the specific number of **cavalrymen** or horsemen that a **Mansabdar** was mandated to maintain for imperial military service.
 
• The **Sawar** rank determined the military strength provided by the official and governed the allowance granted for the upkeep of **horses** and **troopers**.
 
• To ensure the quality of the **Sawar** contingent, the **Mughals** implemented the **Dagh** (branding of horses) and **Chehra** (descriptive rolls of soldiers) systems to prevent fraud and substitution.
 
• The **Sawar** rank could never exceed the **Zat** rank, and the ratio between the two determined the sub-class (first, second, or third) of the **Mansabdar** within their specific grade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zat**

 
 
• This indicated the **personal rank** and status of the officer in the imperial hierarchy.
 
• It was used to calculate the **personal salary** of the **Mansabdar**.
 
 
 
• **Jagir**
 
 
• These were **land revenue assignments** granted to **Mansabdars** in lieu of cash salaries.
 
• The holders, known as **Jagirdars**, collected revenue from these lands to cover their personal pay and the costs of their **Sawar** contingents.
 
 
 
• **Zamindar**
 
 
• Refers to hereditary **landed intermediaries** who had the right to collect land revenue from peasants.
 
• While **Zamindars** provided local stability and collected taxes, they were distinct from **Mansabdars**, who were appointed officials of the **Mughal state**.

questions.question: In April 2025, who has been appointed as the 50th Chief Secretary of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A. Jayathilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A. Jayathilak**, a senior **1991-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** officer, has been designated as the **50th Chief Secretary** of **Kerala**.
 
• He is scheduled to assume the highest administrative office in the state on **April 1, 2025**, succeeding the incumbent official.
 
• He takes over the position from **Sarada Muraleedharan**, who served as the **49th Chief Secretary** and retired from service on **March 31, 2025**.
 
• Prior to this elevation, **A. Jayathilak** served as the **Additional Chief Secretary** for the **Revenue and Disaster Management** and **Taxes** departments.
 
• During his career, he has held several key positions, including **Secretary** of **SC/ST Development**, **Agriculture**, and **Planning**, and also served as the **Chairman** of the **Cochin Port Trust**.
 
• His appointment was finalized by the **Kerala State Cabinet** under the chairmanship of Chief Minister **Pinarayi Vijayan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Secretary Role and Predecessor**:

 
 
• The **Chief Secretary** is the **administrative head** of the state government, acting as the principal advisor to the **Chief Minister** and the **Secretary to the State Cabinet**.
 
• **Sarada Muraleedharan**, whom Jayathilak succeeds, was only the **fifth woman** to hold the post in Kerala’s history.
 
 
 
• **Other Distinguished Entities**:
 
 
• **Sudarshan Venu**: He is the **Managing Director** of **TVS Motor Company** and a prominent leader in the Indian automotive industry.
 
• **S. Mahendra Dev**: An eminent **economist** who served as the **Director** of the **Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)** and Chairman of the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)**.
 
• **Sailesh C. Mehta**: He is the **Chairman and Managing Director** of **Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd**.

questions.question: In May 2025, who has been appointed as the Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Army Command?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lieutenant General Pratik Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lieutenant General Pratik Sharma** has been appointed as the **General Officer Commanding-in-Chief (GOC-in-C)** of the **Northern Army Command** in **May 2025**, succeeding his predecessor in this high-stakes military role.
 
• The **Northern Command** is a **Command-level formation** of the **Indian Army**, which was originally formed in 1908, disbanded in 1947, and re-raised on **June 17, 1972**.
 
• Headquartered at **Udhampur** in the Union Territory of **Jammu and Kashmir**, the command is responsible for managing India's borders with both **Pakistan** and **China** in the northern theater.
 
• The officer in this position oversees critical operational zones, including the **Line of Control (LoC)** in Jammu and Kashmir and the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** in **Ladakh**, ensuring territorial integrity and national security.
 
• The **Northern Command** plays a pivotal role in conducting **counter-insurgency** and **counter-terrorism** operations (such as **Operation Rakshak**) within the region, making it one of the most active operational commands globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Operational Commands of the **Indian Army**:

 
 
• **Western Command**: Headquartered at **Chandimandir**, it manages the borders along Punjab and parts of Rajasthan.
 
• **Eastern Command**: Based in **Kolkata**, it is responsible for the borders with China, Myanmar, and Bangladesh in the northeastern sector.
 
• **Southern Command**: Located in **Pune**, it covers the southern peninsula and the desert sectors of the western border.
 
• **South Western Command**: Headquartered in **Jaipur**, it focuses on the strategic sectors of Rajasthan and Haryana.
 
• **Central Command**: Based in **Lucknow**, it serves as a strategic reserve and oversees the central sector of the border with China.
 
• **Army Training Command (ARTRAC)**: Located in **Shimla**, it is responsible for formulating training doctrines and standards.

questions.question: Which of the following amendment act of Indian constitution gave effect to the acquiring of certain territories by India and transfer of certain other territories to Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100th Amendment act, 2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **100th Amendment Act, 2015** was enacted to give effect to the acquiring of certain territories by India and the transfer of certain other territories to **Bangladesh**.
 
• This constitutional amendment ratified the **Land Boundary Agreement (LBA)** of **1974** and its **2011 Protocol**, which were designed to resolve the long-standing border disputes and the issue of **enclaves** (Chhitmahals).
 
• As a result of this exchange, India transferred **111 enclaves** (covering approximately 17,160 acres) to Bangladesh, while Bangladesh transferred **51 enclaves** (covering approximately 7,110 acres) to India.
 
• The act primarily concerned the **demarcation of boundaries** and the exchange of **adverse possessions** in the border states of **Assam**, **West Bengal**, **Meghalaya**, and **Tripura**.
 
• To implement these territorial changes, the Parliament amended the **First Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**, which lists the states and territories of the Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **91st Amendment Act, 2003**:

 
 
• Restricted the size of the **Council of Ministers** to **15 percent** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly**.
 
• It also strengthened the **Anti-Defection Law** by deleting the provision regarding the protection from disqualification in case of a split by one-third of the members.
 
 
 
• **96th Amendment Act, 2011**:
 
 
• Substituted the name **Odia** for **Oriya** in the **Eighth Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
• This change ensured the official recognition of the correct phonetic pronunciation and spelling of the language.
 
 
 
• **97th Amendment Act, 2011**:
 
 
• Granted constitutional status and protection to **Cooperative Societies**.
 
• It introduced **Part IXB** and **Article 43B** (promotion of cooperative societies) and added the right to form cooperatives under **Article 19**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first Ramsar site of the Jharkhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Udhwa lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary**, situated in the **Sahibganj district**, is the only bird sanctuary in the state of **Jharkhand**.
 
• It consists of two main interconnected water bodies, namely **Patauda Lake** and **Berhale Lake**, spanning an area of about **5.65 square kilometers**.
 
• This natural wetland serves as a crucial habitat for a diverse range of avian species, particularly migratory birds arriving via the **Central Asian Flyway** during winters.
 
• Due to its distinct ecological value and wetland characteristics, it has been proposed as the first potential **Ramsar site** from the state of Jharkhand to receive international recognition under the **Ramsar Convention**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khecheopalri wetland**:

 
 
• Located in the West Sikkim district of **Sikkim**.
 
• It features a sacred lake surrounded by dense forests that holds deep religious significance for both Buddhists and Hindus.
 
 
 
• **Sakkarakottai bird sanctuary**:
 
 
• Located in the **Ramanathapuram district** of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is a designated protected area that acts as an important staging and breeding ground for local and migratory waterbirds.
 
 
 
• **Therthangal bird sanctuary**:
 
 
• Also situated in the **Ramanathapuram district** of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It features a seasonal tank that supports large congregations of nesting bird species like the spot-billed pelican and Painted Stork.

questions.question: The indigenous launch vehicle used in 1980's Indian satellite launching was ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SLV-3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3)** was India's first indigenous experimental satellite launch vehicle, developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• It was a **four-stage** vehicle that used **solid propellant** in all its stages, reaching a height of approximately 22 meters.
 
• On **July 18, 1980**, the SLV-3 successfully deployed the **Rohini satellite (RS-1)** into a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
• With this historic launch, India became the **sixth nation** in the world to possess the capability of launching satellites using its own indigenously developed technology.
 
• The project was led by **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, who served as the **Project Director** and played a pivotal role in the mission's success.
 
• While the initial flight in 1979 was a failure, the subsequent successful launches in the **1980s** (1980 and 1983) paved the way for advanced rocket technology in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ASLV (Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle)**

 
 
• Designed to carry payloads up to **150 kg**.
 
• Developmental flights began in **1987**, but the first successful mission was achieved only in **1992**.
 
 
 
• **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)**
 
 
• Known as the **Workhorse of ISRO**, it is a third-generation launch vehicle.
 
• The first successful launch occurred in **October 1994**.
 
• It was the first Indian launch vehicle to be equipped with **liquid stages**.
 
 
 
• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**
 
 
• A fourth-generation vehicle designed to place heavy satellites into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
• Its maiden flight took place on **April 18, 2001**.
 
• It utilizes the **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)** for high thrust at extreme temperatures.

questions.question: Which institute's researchers developed a water-repellent, conductive textile in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Guwahati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Researchers at the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Guwahati** developed a specialized **water-repellent and conductive textile** in **February 2025**, marking a significant advancement in **material science**.
 
• The textile is engineered to be **superhydrophobic**, meaning it possesses a **water contact angle** greater than 150 degrees, which prevents water from wetting the surface and allows droplets to roll off easily.
 
• By integrating **conductive nanomaterials** onto ordinary fabrics, the researchers created a material that maintains high **electrical conductivity** even while being exposed to moisture or humidity.
 
• The innovation is primarily designed for **smart wearable electronics**, allowing sensors and circuits embedded in clothing to remain functional during rain or heavy perspiration.
 
• This **multi-functional textile** can be used for **human motion sensing**, where it detects minute changes in electrical resistance during physical activities like joint movement or pulse tracking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Textiles and Wearables**:

 
 
• **Conductivity**: Achieved through the application of materials like **carbon nanotubes**, **graphene**, or **conductive polymers** such as **polypyrrole**.
 
• **EMI Shielding**: These textiles can protect against **Electromagnetic Interference**, which is vital for **aerospace** and **defense** applications.
 
• **Durability**: One of the key challenges addressed by the **IIT Guwahati** team was ensuring the **conductive coating** remains stable after multiple **wash cycles** and mechanical stretching.
 
• **Self-Cleaning Property**: The **superhydrophobic** nature provides a **Lotus Effect**, where water droplets carry away dust particles, making the fabric self-cleaning.
 
• **Energy Harvesting**: Future iterations of such textiles may include **triboelectric nanogenerators** to harvest energy from body movements.

questions.question: The Vithalswami Temple is located in ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hampi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vithalswami Temple**, often referred to as the **Vittala Temple**, is an architectural masterpiece located in **Hampi**, **Karnataka**.
 
• The temple was primarily constructed during the **15th century** under the reign of **King Devaraya II** and underwent significant expansions during the rule of **Krishnadevaraya** (1509−1529 CE) of the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• Dedicated to **Lord Vittala**, a manifestation of **Lord Vishnu**, the temple is renowned for its **Dravidian architectural style** and intricate carvings.
 
• One of its most famous features is the **Stone Chariot**, a majestic structure standing in the courtyard, which is now depicted on the reverse side of the **Indian 50 rupee note**.
 
• The temple complex is also celebrated for its **56 musical pillars**, known as **Saptaswara** or **SaReGaMa pillars**, which emit musical notes when struck gently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hampi**:

 
 
• Situated on the banks of the **Tungabhadra River**, it was the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• It is recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** due to its vast collection of ruins and temples.
 
 
 
• **Puri**:
 
 
• Located in **Odisha**, it is famous for the **Jagannath Temple** and the **Ratha Yatra** festival.
 
• It is one of the four **Char Dham** pilgrimage sites in India.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior**:
 
 
• A historic city in **Madhya Pradesh** known for the **Gwalior Fort** and the **Sas-Bahu Temple**.
 
• It has been designated as a **City of Music** by UNESCO.
 
 
 
• **Dispur**:
 
 
• It is the capital of the state of **Assam**, situated within the **Guwahati** metropolitan area.

questions.question: Who is popularly known as 'Loknayak' and was the author of the concept of “Total Revolution”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jayaprakash Narayan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jayaprakash Narayan**, revered as **Loknayak** (Leader of the People), was a preeminent Indian independence activist, social reformer, and political leader.
 
• He conceptualized the idea of **Total Revolution** (Sampoorna Kranti) in 1974, which aimed at a comprehensive transformation of the Indian society across seven spheres: political, social, economic, cultural, ideological, educational, and spiritual.
 
• The **Total Revolution** movement was primarily launched in **Bihar** as a peaceful agitation against corruption, high inflation, and the perceived authoritarianism of the central government led by **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• During the **Quit India Movement** of 1942, he played a legendary role in the underground resistance after his heroic escape from the **Hazaribagh Central Jail**, making him a symbol of socialist activism in India.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian honor, in **1999**, in recognition of his lifelong service to the nation and the cause of democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morarji Desai**:

 
 
• He served as the **4th Prime Minister of India** and led the first non-Congress government under the **Janata Party** in 1977.
 
• He is distinguished as the only Indian citizen to receive both the **Bharat Ratna** and Pakistan's highest civilian award, **Nishan-e-Pakistan**.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra Prasad**:
 
 
• The **first President of India**, he served from 1950 to 1962 and was the President of the **Constituent Assembly**.
 
• He is affectionately known as **Desh Ratna** and **Ajatshatru** for his humble nature and contribution to the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri**:
 
 
• The **second Prime Minister of India**, he is remembered for his leadership during the **Indo-Pakistan War of 1965**.
 
• He gave the iconic slogan **Jai Jawan Jai Kisan** to underscore the importance of soldiers and farmers in nation-building.

questions.question: The Annual Survey of India's City-Systems (ASICS) was published by which of the following?

options.text: Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Annual Survey of India's City-Systems (ASICS)** is a flagship report published by the **Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy**, a **Bengaluru-based** non-profit organization founded in **2001**.
 
• The survey provides a detailed health check of **India's urban governance** by evaluating the 'city-systems' framework, which comprises the laws, policies, institutions, and processes that govern **Indian cities**.
 
• Unlike outcome-oriented rankings like the **Swachh Survekshan** or **Ease of Living Index**, ASICS evaluates the **systemic reforms** necessary to improve service delivery and urban infrastructure.
 
• The report assesses cities across four key pillars: **Urban Planning and Design**, **Urban Capacities and Resources**, **Empowered and Legitimate Political Representation**, and **Transparency, Accountability, and Participation**.
 
• ASICS serves as a diagnostic tool for **policymakers** and **urban practitioners** to identify legal and institutional gaps that hinder effective urban development in major state capitals and metropolitan areas.
 
• The survey often highlights critical issues such as the lack of **financial autonomy** for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), limited powers of **Mayors**, and the shortage of skilled **urban planners** in Indian municipalities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy**:

 
 
• It focuses on transforming the quality of life in **Urban India** through the **City-Systems** framework.
 
• Apart from ASICS, it works on initiatives like **I Change My City** and programs related to **Municipal Finance** and **Civic Learning**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• The premier policy think tank of the **Government of India**, established on **1 January 2015**.
 
• It publishes various indices such as the **SDG India Index**, **School Education Quality Index**, and **State Health Index**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**:
 
 
• The nodal ministry for the welfare of **Scheduled Castes**, **Backward Classes**, **Persons with Disabilities**, and the **Elderly**.
 
• It implements acts like the **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016**.

questions.question: Which of the following countries rank 79th in the Global Business Complexity Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Cayman Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Business Complexity Index (GBCI)** is an annual comprehensive report published by the **TMF Group**, analyzing the administrative and regulatory environments of **79 jurisdictions** that account for the majority of the world's **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and **GDP**.
 
• In the **2024/2025** ranking cycle, the **Cayman Islands** is ranked at the **79th position**, identifying it as the **least complex** jurisdiction globally for business operations.
 
• The index measures complexity across three core areas: **Accounting and Tax**, **HR and Payroll**, and **Global Entity Management** (incorporation and compliance).
 
• The **Cayman Islands** maintains this ranking due to its **tax-neutral** status, lack of **direct corporate taxes**, and highly efficient **regulatory framework** designed to facilitate international financial services.
 
• The **GBCI** utilizes over **290 indicators** to determine the ease or difficulty of operating in a specific country, focusing on the time and cost required to comply with **local laws**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Complexity Trends:**

 
 
• Countries like **Greece**, **France**, and **Colombia** are typically found at the top of the index, representing the **highest complexity** due to frequent legislative changes and intricate **labor laws**.
 
• The **Netherlands** is recognized for its **digitalization** and **transparency**, often ranking in the lower half of the index, signifying a relatively **friendly business environment**.
 
• **Norway** maintains low complexity through its advanced **technological infrastructure** and the **Altinn** portal, which streamlines reporting for businesses.
 
• **Mauritius** remains a preferred **investment gateway** for **Africa**, utilizing its **Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs)** and simple **incorporation processes** to attract global entities.
 
• The **GBCI** report highlights that **geopolitical tensions** and **inflationary pressures** are currently the primary drivers of **regulatory shifts** in most developed jurisdictions.
